acceptance.statement: All twelve canonical loops emit current tenant-scoped controller records that satisfy the shared controller-record contract and read back through the BFF under the authenticated tenant and environment.
The BFF shows desired-state presence, controller health, last success, last failure, downstream actual state, and provenance for every loop.
Stale, absent, and contradicted records remain unaccepted and visibly degraded for every loop, with a specific rejection reason.

Catalog controller names, queries, restart behavior, and liveness fields match the implementation, checked in both directions: a catalog claim without a deployed controller fails, and a deployed controller absent from the catalog fails.

Maturity is no higher than implemented until hosted evidence is admitted: no catalog loop declares reconciled or proven-live maturity, a proven_live controller contract, or present live evidence, and zero loops are admitted as live by the read model.

actual_state: domain terminal actual-state observation carried on the controller record
desired_state: domain desired-state observation carried on the controller record

proof: The controller record identity key remains (tenant_id, environment, loop_id); this task adds no new write path.

test_every_canonical_loop_record_conforms_and_reads_back_tenant_scoped feeds one record per loop plus a second consultation record scoped to another tenant, and asserts the foreign record's evidence ref never appears on any projected loop.

test_stale_and_contradicted_records_stay_unaccepted_for_every_loop drives all twelve loops through three refusal cases: a stale heartbeat, archive-only evidence refs, and contradicted evidence provenance.

In every case controller_health.current_record_accepted is false, evidence_packet.accepted_live_liveness is false, and operator_truth.degraded is true, with a specific rejection_reason on each loop whose catalog contract is implemented.
The loop-health surface reports status degraded and controller_health_record_count 0 for the stale case rather than hiding the loops.

Each projected loop carries evidence_packet.source, runtime_record_evidence_basis, runtime_evidence_refs, and highest_truth_level, so an operator can trace a displayed value back to the controller record that produced it.
archived_task_completion_accepted stays false on every loop, so task-archive completion is visible as reference-only and never as runtime correlation.

The catalog now records each implemented controller's restart_behavior, and test_loop_catalog_controller_contract_matches_runtime_implementation asserts the named controller module actually contains the durable state-path environment variable and identity-refresh symbols that behavior describes: SOURCE_INGEST_CONTROLLER_STATE_PATH and refresh_runtime_identity for source_ingestion, DISTILLATION_CONTROLLER_STATE_PATH and refresh_runtime_identity for strategy_distillation, and ALPHA_REPLICATION_CONTROLLER_STATE_PATH for alpha_replication.

A controller restart produces a fresh heartbeat; the read model accepts a record only inside the 900 second freshness window, and the negative control that widened that window was caught by the all-loop staleness test.

Controller restart and recovery behavior itself is owned and proved by L12-CTRL-001 and L12-MANIFEST-RESTART-PROOF-20260729; this task binds the catalog's description of it to the code that implements it.
The delivery is a static catalog change plus read-model and test changes; reverting the task commits restores the previous catalog exactly.
No stored data is migrated and no runtime write path is altered, so there is nothing to compensate.
